turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall endeavour to do so, ma’am. But… but the door seems rather far, and I’m afraid I might stumble, and… and cause some disturbance. I do hope I won’t be causing you any further… any further trouble.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disturbance? Oh, a little stumble, a little tremor… those are merely echoes, dear boy, of a far greater fall. Go, Pip, do as I ask. Call Estella. She understands… she understands the delicate dance of disappointment.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I truly shall, ma’am. It’s just… the shadows are rather deep there, and I wouldn't wish to… to speak too loudly, lest I should… disturb something. Forgive me, Miss Havisham, I’m merely… anxious to please.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Anxious to please? Such a commendable sentiment, Pip. But pleasing me is a… a peculiar art, is it not? It requires a certain… boldness, a willingness to pierce the veil of sorrow, even if the shards cut you. Call Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. A peculiar art… yes, I… I apprehend your meaning. Perhaps… perhaps if I were to proceed with a little more… haste, I might avoid… further… further observation of the shadows?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Haste, you say? Haste is a vulgarity, Pip, a desperate attempt to outrun time—as if one *could*. No, no, linger a moment longer in the gloom. It is in the shadows that truths are revealed, even if those truths are… devastating.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, Miss Havisham... I… I shall endeavour to linger, as you request. But the gloom… it presses rather heavily, and I confess, my imagination does sometimes… run away with me. I shall call for Estella presently, I believe.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Imagination, you say? A most dangerous faculty, Pip, particularly when unrestrained by reason. It conjures phantoms, breeds anxieties... and what is my existence *but* a phantom, a breeding ground for anxieties?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Phantoms, you say, Miss Havisham? I… I try, you see, to keep a firm grasp on reality, but this house… it lends itself to such… such fanciful notions. Perhaps calling for Estella will provide a… a diversion from them, a focus for my… my attention.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A diversion, Pip? A pretty word, that. But diversions, like smiles, are fleeting, are they not? They mask the emptiness, the… the *lack* of something vital.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: A… a lack, Miss Havisham? Indeed, a most unfortunate state. I… I daresay, perhaps, if Estella were present, she might… she might offer a perspective that I, in my… my limited understanding, am quite unable to grasp.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A perspective, Pip? You believe Estella possesses a perspective I lack? My dear boy, you flatter her, and perhaps, inadvertently, me. But perspectives, like hope, are fragile things, easily shattered by the harsh light of truth... and truth, as I have learned, is a most unwelcome visitor.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I wouldn't presume to suggest that Miss Havisham lacks perspective, certainly not. It is merely that… that perhaps a fresh viewpoint, however slight, might… might offer a momentary respite from… from the weight of things, you understand. I only wish to be helpful, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Helpful, you say? A sweet ambition, Pip, but I suspect you mistake my desires. Do you believe a mere shift in focus, a fleeting glimpse of another’s face, can truly lift the burden of years? No, my dear boy, the weight remains, pressing down, always pressing down…

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I believe you are quite right, Miss Havisham. It is a foolish notion of mine, to imagine that such trivialities as I could offer could alleviate such… such profound sorrow. Forgive me, I only wished to be agreeable, and I fear I have proven myself to be quite inadequate.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Inadequate, am I? Yes, you are astute, Pip. I am inadequate, perpetually so, to mend a heart shattered into a thousand irreparable pieces. But tell me, child, do you see the dust? Do you see how it settles, a perpetual shroud, upon everything I hold dear?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, Miss Havisham, I do observe the dust; it is… quite pervasive, isn't it? It coats everything, a melancholy testament to the passage of time, and… and to the stillness that seems to have settled upon this entire place.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Stillness… yes, you perceive it, Pip. It is a stillness born of expectation, a stillness that echoes with the silence of vows broken, a silence that… that consumes me, you see. It is a terrible, beautiful silence, isn't it?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It… it is a most peculiar stillness, Miss Havisham, certainly. One feels… one feels almost as though one ought to be very quiet, lest one disturb… disturb something very important that is suspended in the air.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Suspended, you say? Yes, quite. As if a breath, a single, fragile breath, could shatter the illusion, Pip. I find myself clinging to this stillness, you understand, for within it, within this quiet despair, lies the faint echo of what *might* have been.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
